headline: Preprint reports forced-choice answer formats suppress refusal mechanisms in hazardous-knowledge evaluations
summary: An arXiv preprint published on 2026-11-05 compares multiple-choice and open-ended versions of WMDP questions on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. The authors report that models often answer forced-choice hazardous-knowledge questions even when they refuse matched open-ended questions, and present tuned-lens, refusal-direction and attention-head interventions as a mechanistic account. The causal head-ablation result is robust on Llama-3.1-8B but not Qwen3-8B. These are author-reported preprint results; no independent replication was inspected.
